carol: Heads up — after the RBAC tighten that landed ~17:02 UTC we're seeing internal inference client errors in eu-west and ap-south. Error rate spiked ~3% -> 18% for internal /v1/generate calls. Looks like mTLS resumption paths are failing and fallbacks aren't being logged.

ben: Any example logs? can you paste a small sampling?

carol: paste from proxy logs:
```
2026-06-05T17:06:12Z proxy[ingress-eu]: TLS handshake failed: session ticket decrypt failed: KMS decrypt denied for key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:...
2026-06-05T17:06:12Z proxy[ingress-eu]: client=svc-inference, route=/v1/generate, src=10.11.12.13, err="tls: session ticket unmarshal: decrypt error"
```

alice: I see matching KMS denies in the audit stream:
```
2026-06-05T17:05:59Z KMS Audit: Deny | principal=service-keystore-rotator | action=Decrypt | resource=alias/redwood-keystore-eu | reason=iam:Decrypt not authorized (rbac change applied)
```

alice: RBAC policy that was pushed removed the `kms:Decrypt` for the intermediate keystore role in eu-west/ap-south. It was meant to scope privileges, but the proxy expects keystore access during session ticket unwrap.

dmitri: Runtime behavior note — we intentionally treat session-ticket unwrap failures as fatal and reject resumption. That avoids silent fallback to weaker handshakes, but in this case the failure is caused by an auth policy change, not an attacker.

ben: So two issues: RBAC removed decrypt rights -> KMS denies -> session ticket unwrap fails -> resumption rejected -> requests fall back to 0-RTT/full handshake path which we also disable by default -> 5xx. Also our observability didn't tag the chain as RBAC/KMS failure specifically.

carol: Can we quickly (A) restore kms:Decrypt for the keystore role in eu-west/ap-south (B) enable a temporary runtime fallback to accept full handshake when ticket unwrap fails and log the real cause, and (C) flip on `tls.session.debug=audit` to capture better reasons?

alice: I can revert the policy in IAM; need ~6min review for cross-team signoff.

ben: I'll open an incident and do the runtime quick patch. On runtime side we can change behavior to treat ticket unwrap failure as "log + fallback to full handshake" for 30m and ship via a canary to eu-west. That avoids a global rollback.
deploy-bot: deployment:runtime/accept-full-handshake-fallback v2026.06.05-canary -> canary eu-west started (id=deploy-8793)

carol: After canary started error rate in eu-west dropped back to ~2%. ap-south still has failures (RBAC not yet reverted there).

alice: ap-south policy revert in progress, pinging infra, ETA ~12m.

ben: @sre_oncall can you take on alert routing and notify product owners? Will also add a short-term rule to route inference traffic away from nodes that fail keystore unwrap to dedicated fallback pool.

sre_oncall: Got it. I'm creating an incident: INC-2026-1893, pageing the oncall and owners. I'll add the temporary routing rule.

dmitri: Follow-ups: 1) make session unwrap failures emit structured audit events (keystore request id, KMS response code) 2) add a guard in the keystore agent to assert RBAC change impact during deploys (fail-fast to avoid stealth outages) 3) add regional canary for RBAC policy changes that touch keystore roles.

carol: Agreed. Also we should add a short runbook step: if you see `session ticket decrypt failed` -> check KMS Deny logs for `iam:Decrypt` and revert RBAC change or rotate a short-lived grant.

alice: Policy revert applied for ap-south and eu-west. KMS denies stop at 17:18 UTC.

ben: Can confirm error rates back to baseline in both regions. Rolling back the runtime fallback in 30m after monitoring.

carol: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a postmortem doc and a checklist to include RBAC-impact smoke tests for keystore dependencies. :thumbsup:
